summary: Iteration 11 backend-only retest of _client_ip() (walks XFF from the right, skipping invalid, private/loopback, Cloudflare IPv4, Google LB 35.191.0.0/16 and 130.211.0.0/22, and TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS entries). The iteration_10 HIGH finding is FIXED. Over the public URL, one machine sending malformed XFF 'x' now gets exactly 5x 401, then 429 (probe: 5 of 24 attempts returned 401; it was 20 in iteration_10). Also 429 for 'a, b, c, d', '35.191.1.1', 'x, 1.2.3.4', '::1, junk' and '999.1.1.1', even with the correct password. Rotating valid spoofed XFF gives 5x 401, then 429. A different real client (internal crafted chain, including a chain with a trailing 35.191.x GFE hop and junk) is not locked out and gets 200. The pod egress key is locked (429) whatever spoof is prepended. Junk, private and extra 130.211/35.191 hops in the chain do not change the key. All-private chain or no XFF falls back to client.host. A success resets that client's own counter. The per-token cap of 20 across IPs still gives 429, including on the public path. Share rate-limit suite: 17/17 passed. Full backend regression: 100 passed, 1 skipped (the last-admin guard is skipped because 2 admins exist).

minor.issue: Code review, not exploited live. The whole Cloudflare IPv4 list is skipped at ANY position. If the real client hop itself is a Cloudflare IP, it is skipped and the next client-supplied entry to its left becomes the key, which is spoofable. Examples: users or attackers on Cloudflare WARP/1.1.1.1 (egress 104.28.x.x, inside 104.24.0.0/14) or requests sent from a Cloudflare Worker. Such an attacker can rotate the left XFF entry to get 20 tries and trip the per-token cap, which is the all-guest 15-min lockout from iteration_10, but only for CF-origin clients. Brute force stays bounded at 20 per 15 min. Mitigation: skip CF ranges only for the expected CF egress hop (at most one CF entry to the right of the real-client hop), then take the next valid entry as-is.

No Cloudflare IPv6 ranges. If the CF egress hop is ever IPv6 (e.g. 2a06:98c0::/29 or 2400:cb00::/32), it would be taken as the client key and would rotate per request, so the per-IP limit would be bypassed again. Every egress observed so far was IPv4. Add the CF IPv6 list for robustness.
Still in-memory and per-worker, and it resets on restart (known, unchanged).
